main_text.p: potest sacerdotem illum legem attulisse, non aliis characteribus descriptam, quam quibus Israelitæ à Mose ad illum usque diem usi fuerant: ab eo autem tempore Samaritanos antiquis literis Hebraicis, saltem in lege describenda, usos fuisse nulla est ratio cur dubitemus. Postea constat, ex Neh.13.4.28. Et Josephi Antiq.l.11.c.7,8. Manasse Jaddi Pontificis fratrem eo quod repudiare nollet uxore quâ duxerat filiâ Sanballati Samariæ præfecti, sacerdotio exutu ad socerū confugisse, qui templum alterum in monte Gerizim construxit, Hierosolymitano simile, in quo Manasses sacerdotio functus est apud Samaritanos, & quidem ritibus Mosaicis secundum legem (quâ habuisse eos & servâsse vero consentaneum est) et ad ipsum multi ex Judæis confugerunt qui reforma-tioni ab Esrafastæ se submittere nollent. Hinc schisma & dissidium magis invaluit, utrisque legem Mosis profitentibus & se mutuo anathe-mate ferientibus, hocque non tantum stante utroque templo, sed & post utrumq; vastatum, & utri-usq; partis sequaces cum tota gente dissipatos: adeo ut non liceret Judæo cum Cuthæo seu Samaritano panem comedere, juxta adagium, Qui comedit panem Samariticum, æque est ac si comederet carnem suillam. Refertque Drusius de 3. Sectis Judæorum. lib.3.c. 11. ex Tanchuma, solennem excommunicationem Samaritanorum jactam ab Ezra & Nehemia.

p.i: 17.Habent itaq; Samaritani Mosis Pentateu-chum, quem ad hunc usque diem in Sichem, Da-masco, aliisque locis ubi habitant ipsorum reliquiæ, publicè legunt, antiquis characteribus descriptum, quique non multum differt ab hodi-erno.

page.notes: Italic type is judged from the scan and may be partly wrong in the 17. paragraph and the Drusius sentence. Uncertain readings: "Jaddi" (the printed name may be Iaddi or Jaddua; the letter looks like f/s), "Esrafastæ" (the printed name is hard to read), "jactam" (the printed word is ligatured and could be read differently), "11" for the book/chapter number (printed as an old form, read as 11). "Socerū" uses a macron over u as printed. The short strokes at the right ends of some lines are printing marks, not text, and are not transcribed. The catchword "erno" is at the foot right and matches "hodi-" at the line end.
